objective: Trace how HolyAgent picks the screen capability's form (normal, headless) and how it detects and grants T3 Code's browser preview tools, to tell whether a session inside T3 Code can get the headless browser server instead of, or beside, the T3 browser.
scope: Read in /home/user/holyagent-0.3.2-fff (stable tree; its headless form still names the Playwright MCP server, which the browser-use branch replaces one for one) and, for the browser-use registration only, /home/user/holyagent-0.3.2-browser-use/packages/integrations/pi/src/screen.ts and packages/runtime/src/config/capabilities.ts (that tree is being edited; read, do not rely on line numbers).

Answer: 1. Where and how the form is chosen (setup time or session time; signals such as display, CI, cloud, a config key). 2. How T3 Code is detected (env vars, host flag) and which tools a screen specialist gets in T3 (T3 preview and HTML render tools; refuseT3PreviewOutsideT3 in screen.ts). 3. In a T3 Code session, can the headless server be registered and granted to screen specialists, together with or instead of the T3 tools? Give the code path with file:line. 4. Any existing doc (docs/pi/screen.md, docs on T3) describing the T3 browser and how its preview tools reach it (an MCP server, an API, CDP).
constraints: Read only; make no edits and no git writes.
Report in under 400 words, with file:line for each claim.

criteria.text: Each of the four questions is answered with file:line evidence or marked not found

result:
result: Your claim is partly right. Both browsers are already granted together, and in a T3 session the headless server can be registered beside the T3 tools. It cannot replace them without code changes. Form selection is machine-based, so a desktop T3 session gets browse (normal form), not the headless server. All paths below are under /home/user/holyagent-0.3.2-fff unless stated otherwise.

1. Form choice (session time, no config key)
- `packages/runtime/src/setup/form.ts:53-60` `detectForm` checks, in order: claude.ai cloud session -> headless; truthy `CI` -> headless; no `DISPLAY`/`WAYLAND_DISPLAY` on Linux -> headless (`hasDisplay` at :33-36); otherwise normal.
- `--form` overrides it (`chooseForm`, :63-70) in setup and doctor only.
- The dispatch calls `detectForm(call.env)` at `packages/runtime/src/cli/assignment.ts:268`.
- The dispatch prints the agent name: `<role>-screen` or `<role>-headless-screen`. The specialist reads its form from that name (`screenFormOf`, `packages/integrations/pi/src/screen.ts:51-52`; `extension.ts:1053`).
- Not found: no per-session config key forces headless on a desktop. Only `--form` (setup/doctor) or the env vars above do.

2. T3 detection and tools
- `packages/integrations/pi/src/t3.ts:38-42` `isT3Session`: Pi `mode === "rpc"` AND a non-blank `T3_PI_RUNTIME_MODE` or `T3_MCP_URL`.
- Preview tools: `T3_PREVIEW_TOOLS` at `packages/runtime/src/config/capabilities.ts:204-209` are `preview_*`, `t3_preview_*`, `html_render` and `html_preview`.
- They are granted via the `mcp` capability's `tools.screen` (:415). The visual roles also get `device_*` through `T3_VISUAL_TOOLS` (:216).
- `refuseT3PreviewOutsideT3` (`screen.ts:85-97`) blocks these calls for a screen specialist when `!t3`. It is wired at `extension.ts:1620`.

3. Headless server beside or instead of T3
- Beside: yes, and this is the current design.
  - `docs/pi/screen.md:19` says the headless agent file lists the Playwright tools and the T3 preview tools. The `mcp` row at :66 gives the same T3 grant in both forms.
  - `registerScreen` (`extension.ts:1396-1417`) calls `registerScreenServers` (`screen.ts:110-141`) via `pi.registerMcpServer`, using `screenServers(config, form)` (`screen.ts:62-77`).
  - Those servers come from the enabled capabilities for the form, and the `browser-use` headless form carries the server. The T3 tools come from T3's own bridge, injected independently of this path.
- Instead of: not possible today.
  - The `mcp` capability's `screen` grant is unconditional (:415).
  - The form is machine-derived, so a T3 desktop session gets `browse` (`screen.md:65`), not headless.
  - To force headless in T3, I would add an override of `detectForm` / `screenFormOf` (for example when `isT3Session`). I would drop `T3_PREVIEW_TOOLS` from `screen` or from the agent file, and `refuseT3PreviewOutsideT3` would need no change. This is a hypothesis; I did not run it.

Browser-use tree (read only; line numbers may move)
- `/home/user/holyagent-0.3.2-browser-use/packages/runtime/src/config/capabilities.ts:493-528`: the headless form registers `BROWSER_USE_MCP_SERVER`, which runs `uvx browser-use --cli-mcp` and attaches to a Chromium started by `holyagent browser-server` (:332-339). Its tools are `browser_exec` and `browser_screenshot` (:292-293).
- The same file keeps `T3_PREVIEW_TOOLS` in the `mcp` capability's screen grant (:454).
- `.../pi/src/screen.ts:30,37` keeps the T3 preview tools in the headless note ("where T3 hosts the session").
- So the branch replaces Playwright with browser-use one for one and does not touch the T3 path.

4. Docs on how T3's preview tools reach its browser
- `docs/pi/t3-code.md:45`: T3 injects its own MCP bridge extension (`pi --mode rpc --extension <t3 mcp ext>` with `T3_MCP_URL` and `T3_MCP_BEARER_TOKEN`), which routes to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp` with a per-session credential.
- `docs/pi/t3-code.md:89`: `preview_*` is the integrated browser; the doc keeps it for the visual specialists.
- `docs/pi/t3-code.md:168` mentions `mcpInjection`.
- `docs/pi/screen.md:3-24`: the T3 preview tools sit in the `mcp` capability.
- Gap: no doc says how T3's preview drives its browser internally (CDP or another route). I only read that the tools are reached over MCP.

notes: The T3 browser is a view into T3's own page (`screen.ts:81-83`). It is not a general browser-use backend. Making it the backend means building an MCP-to-T3-preview adapter, and nothing in the repo shows T3 exposing CDP. I did not verify whether T3 exposes CDP.

evidence:
Each of the four questions is answered with file:line evidence or marked not found: Q1 form.ts:33-70, assignment.ts:268, screen.ts:51-52. Q2 t3.ts:38-42, capabilities.ts:204-216,415, screen.ts:85-97. Q3 extension.ts:1396-1417, 1620, screen.ts:62-141, screen.md:19,65-66, plus browser-use tree capabilities.ts:493-528. Q4 t3-code.md:45,89 and screen.md. Not found: a per-session config key forcing the form, and any doc of T3's internal browser transport (CDP).
findings: see the answers 1-4 above.
